notes: A DOCSIS 3.1 cable modem with two gigabit Ethernet ports and one coax connector. The chip details are for the board DeviWiki records as PCB ARCT04227 (silkscreen RevM); other board revisions may use other chips.

gaps: Board revision: DeviWiki's chip list is for PCB ARCT04227 (silkscreen PWB:597403-001 RevM, dated 2016-10-20). Other revisions were not read.
RAM: DeviWiki gives 3 GiB on two chips, shown as brand and model unknown. No second source was found for the amount or the chips.
The flash part numbers (Spansion S34ML01G200TFV00, Macronix MX25L12835FZ2I-10G) and the 12 VDC 2 A adapter rating come from DeviWiki only, which does not say what type of flash either chip is.
Adapter current: the user guide and quick start show a +12VDC connector but give no current. A SURFboard community answer was not readable (the link redirects to the SURFboard home page).
FCC ID: DeviWiki says none available, so the fcc field is left empty.

Radio and antenna 'absent' entries dropped: no source that could be read says the modem has no Wi-Fi. The ARRIS documents describe two Ethernet ports and a coax connector, and SpeedGuide's table has no wireless section.
Chips named but not claimed: Maxim MAX3522 RF amplifier (DeviWiki, qty 1). No part type in the guide fits an RF amplifier.
LEDs: the ARRIS spec sheet lists front LEDs as Power, US/DS and Online plus Ethernet link LEDs on the rear; the quick start and user guide show four front LEDs (Power, Receive, Send, Online).

Production years: none of the sources read gives them. The user guide is dated August 2016, the spec sheet carries a 2016 copyright and the quick start is dated November 2019; these are document dates.
The AP3432 datasheet (Diodes) is marked part obsolete, no alternate part.
Refused or unreadable: Newegg listing (HTTP 403) and SURFboard community (redirect), both to the checker.
method: ARRIS SURFboard SB8200 DOCSIS 3.1 product spec sheet, hosted by Cable One (PDF, read with the research tool): interfaces, LEDs, Ethernet and F connector.

ARRIS SURFboard SB8200 Cable Modem User Guide, PN 365-095-30000 x.2, August 2016, hosted by Midco (PDF, read with the research tool): rear-panel table with the +12VDC connector and power-supply warning, front-panel LED table.
ARRIS SB8200 quick start guide, ARSVD01676-e 11/2019, hosted by Cox (PDF, read with the research tool): front-panel LED table (Power, Receive, Send, Online).
DeviWiki Arris SB8200 page (community wiki, readable without a bot check): BCM3390Z, flash, RAM, power, connector type, additional chips, PCB markings.
SpeedGuide Arris SB8200 page (readable): chipset listed as Broadcom BCM3390, two gigabit Ethernet ports and a coax WAN port. Cross-check only.
Datasheets read with the research tool: AP3432 (Diodes, DS42622 Rev. 1-4) and TPS65276V (TI, SLVSBW0B, January 2014); both name the chip on page 1.
Refused to the researcher: Tenable's Medium teardown (HTTP 403), TechInfoDepot (Anubis bot check).

comps.spec: Broadcom BCM3390Z (DeviWiki's CPU field); DeviWiki also lists it as the Ethernet and switch chip, and SpeedGuide gives the chipset as Broadcom BCM3390
RAM on two chips, 3 GiB in total (DeviWiki; it shows brand and model as unknown)
BCD Semiconductor AP3432 1.5 MHz step-down DC-DC converter, 2.5 A (DeviWiki)
Texas Instruments TPS65276V dual step-down converter, three listed on DeviWiki
12 VDC power adapter, 2 A (DeviWiki: power 12 VDC, 2 A)
One external F-type coax connector (cable input)
+12VDC power connector on the rear panel; the user guide warns to use only the power supply provided in the box
Four front-panel status LEDs: Power, Receive, Send and Online. Green when connected; Receive and Send turn blue for bonded DOCSIS 3.1 channels
